summary: Iteration 50 — bulk-add honesty + Membership + Delete warning + complimentary regression. BACKEND (pytest /app/backend/tests/test_iteration50_bulk_and_membership.py — 12/12 passed in 12.15s; the iteration-49 complimentary suite also replayed 12/12 for a 24/24 pass, JUnit /app/test_reports/pytest/pytest_iteration50.xml). FREE_ITEM_CAP root cause reproduced + verified: for a brand-new /auth/register account stripped of complimentary/premium fields in Mongo, pre-seeded with 100 items on its default profile, POST /api/capture returns 200 while THREE back-to-back POST /api/items calls each return 402 with detail 'Free wardrobes hold up to 100 pieces. Delete a piece to free a slot, or go Premium for unlimited.' and GET /api/items?summary=1 still returns exactly 100 — NO partial/orphan writes. Granting revenuecat premium lets the same account save the 101st item (count → 101). A fresh complimentary account (default state) can also save past 100. POST /api/items with no photo returns 400 'A photo is required to add an item.' premium_plan label verified on /auth/me AND /membership/plans: 'aureve_annual_v1' → 'Annual', 'aureve_monthly_v1' → 'Monthly', 'aureve_lifetime_v1' → 'Premium' (fallback); null for complimentary and free. Iteration-49 complimentary intact — fresh register → 6–7 days remaining, re-login does not restart complimentary_expires_at. Reviewer user_testaura01 was snapshotted before/after and remains premium_until=2099-01-01, premium_source='revenuecat'. FRONTEND (web @ 390x844, EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL): THE CRITICAL BULK FLOW IS CORRECT. Logged in as a throwaway non-premium account with a pre-seeded 100-item wardrobe, /bulk-add → Choose photos → playwright file-chooser handed 3 real JPEGs → bulk-result-title reads '0 pieces added', bulk-result-sub reads "We couldn't add these items. Please try again.", each of the 3 failed tiles shows 'Couldn't add' + the full 402 cap message 'Free wardrobes hold up to 100 pieces. Delete a piece to free a slot, or go Premium for unlimited.', the stale 'All set — they're in your wardrobe now.' copy is NOT shown, bulk-retry-failed and bulk-go-premium are BOTH present, and GET /api/items?summary=1 still returns 100 (no items created). Tapping bulk-retry-failed re-ran the three photos WITHOUT re-opening the picker (3 new 402s logged in console), title stayed at '0 pieces added', count stayed at 100. Then flipping the same account to revenuecat premium + wiping the 100 fillers and uploading 2 fresh photos produced bulk-result-title '2 pieces added' + bulk-result-sub 'All set — they're in your wardrobe now.' with NO retry/go-premium buttons; GET /api/items?summary=1 returned 2 real items (also with meaningful AI-generated names like 'Magenta top'). A mixed-batch 'X of Y pieces added' assertion was NOT exercised in the web preview (a non-premium 101st in the middle of a batch would need the server state to flip mid-run, which isn't practical with the current test harness) — reported here rather than failing the suite. Profile MEMBERSHIP section: logged in as review@aureve.app the paid-membership-row renders with 'Premium Membership' + 'Renews / expires 1/1/2099' + manage-subscription labelled 'Manage / Cancel Subscription' (web manageSubscription() correctly routes to /premium); only ONE of the three member cards is in the DOM (complimentary-row + free-membership-row + go-premium + see-premium-plans all absent). Switching the token to <set via the TEST_SESSION_TOKEN environment variable> (user_testaura01, premium_source=revenuecat, revenuecat_product=null → premium_plan='Premium') also shows paid-membership-row AND the extra 'Current plan: Premium' line — confirming the premium_plan wiring reaches the UI. Delete Account: tapping delete-account on the paid reviewer account opens the confirm modal with delete-subscription-warning AND delete-manage-subscription both present, plus confirm-delete and cancel-delete; dismissed via cancel-delete so the reviewer account was NEVER deleted. The complimentary-account 'no warning' path was NOT re-verified visually in iteration 50 because iteration 49 already covered it (profile.tsx line 290 gates the warning on `premium && !user?.complimentary_active`), reported as a code-review confirmation rather than a re-screenshotted check. REGRESSION: single POST /items with a photo still 200s + persists; wardrobe count moves 0→2 after bulk success; Home complimentary pill still shows for a brand-new account (iteration-49 pytest replayed). Only pre-existing warnings in console ('shadow*' + 'pointerEvents' deprecations). No red screens. All throwaway accounts DELETE /auth/account'd by the pytest fixtures and the manual UI run; review@aureve.app and user_testaura01 confirmed byte-identical to the credentials file after testing.

minor.issue: Substring matcher includes 'mo' and '1m', which is extremely loose — any product id containing those two chars (e.g. 'aureve_promo_lifetime', '*mo*nument', '1morebonus') is classified as 'Monthly'. For current product ids ('aureve_monthly_v1', 'aureve_annual_v1') it works fine, but tightening to word-boundary/explicit tokens ('_mo_', 'monthly', '_1m_') would prevent future product-id typos from being mislabelled. Flagging rather than failing — behaviour for the three canonical ids is correct.

action_items: OPTIONAL (not blocking): tighten premium_plan_label matcher so 'mo'/'1m' aren't bare substrings — use explicit tokens like 'monthly', '_1m_' or regex word-boundaries so unusual product ids can't be mislabelled 'Monthly'.
critical_code_review_comments: /app/frontend/app/bulk-add.tsx:60-114 processImages correctly: tracks a per-row rowIdx so cleaned thumbnails always land on the originating tile; only pushes to the `created` list when createdItem.id actually exists; captures failureReason(e) + blocked flag + src (original base64) on every failure, so a 402 cap tile shows the real server message rather than the swallowed 'All set' copy that used to leak out.

/app/frontend/app/bulk-add.tsx:171-181 retryFailed replays only the failed photos (filtered via r.status==='failed' && r.src) WITHOUT calling pickMultipleFromLibrary — verified end-to-end in the UI (3 fresh 402s on retry, no file-picker reopening).

/app/frontend/app/bulk-add.tsx:187-201 the three honest states derive from counts (added/failed/attempted + 'blocked' derived from any row with a 402 flag), so bulk-go-premium only appears when the failure was a gate; mixed-batch copy 'X of Y pieces added' + '{failed} didn't save…' is correctly wired even though we could not force a real mixed-run in the web preview.

/app/frontend/app/(tabs)/profile.tsx:200-246 — exactly one of complimentary-row / paid-membership-row / free-membership-row renders, driven by user.complimentary_active and the usePremiumAccess hook; the paid-row 'Current plan' line is conditional on user.premium_plan truthiness, and manage-subscription routes to /premium on web via manageSubscription() (lines 62-73), which is the documented fallback.

/app/frontend/app/(tabs)/profile.tsx:290-300 — delete-subscription-warning + delete-manage-subscription are gated on `premium && !user?.complimentary_active`, which is exactly the paid-member rule the review asks for: complimentary users do NOT see the Apple-subscription warning, paid revenuecat/reviewer users do. (Note: reviewer accounts with premium_source='reviewer' also trip this because `premium` is true and complimentary is false — which is the correct, conservative behaviour; the backend has no 'this is a seeded reviewer' flag to differentiate from a real paid user, and showing the warning to a reviewer-type account is harmless because the Manage link safely routes to /premium on web and to the StoreKit sheet on device.)

/app/backend/server.py:275-284 premium_plan_label returns None unless premium_source=='revenuecat', so complimentary / reviewer / free all read null — the UI's `{user?.premium_plan ? …}` branch therefore stays hidden for those states, which is exactly the review requirement.

/app/backend/server.py:1487-1514 create_item: has_image check is FIRST (so a photoless payload is a clean 400 before touching the cap); FREE_ITEM_CAP(100) gate is behind `not user.get('account_premium')`, so complimentary + revenuecat + reviewer all bypass it; the gate uses count_documents(items_scope(user)) which already filters by profile_id, so family profiles share the account-level cap. 402 raises before any db.items.insert_one, hence the 'no orphan documents' invariant we verified in test_101st_item_returns_402_and_count_stays_100.

rca_of_issue: RCA was already captured in the problem statement (old bulk screen hard-coded the success copy and swallowed per-item reasons, so a 100-cap non-premium wardrobe always read 'All set' with 0 real adds). The fix is correct and now verified end-to-end: bulk-add.tsx failureReason(e) categorises status 402 as a gate (blocked:true) and stores the server detail as the row.reason; doneTitle/doneSub derive from added/failed/attempted so '0 pieces added' + 'We couldn't add these items. Please try again.' only shows when added===0 && failed>0, 'X of Y pieces added' only shows for partial, and 'All set — they're in your wardrobe now' only shows when failed===0. Row-indexed cleaning (`created.push({id, rowIdx})`) prevents the previous bug where cleaned thumbnails could land on the wrong tile in a mixed batch. The item-exists check (`if (!createdItem?.id) throw …`) prevents counting a tile as added without a real wardrobe id.
